hook: Jürgen Schmidhuber was born in Munich, Germany, and earned his doctorate in computer science from the Technical University of Munich in 1991. In 1990 he proposed an early adversarial training scheme in which two neural networks competed against each other, an idea later recognized as anticipating generative adversarial networks. In 1997 he and his student Sepp Hochreiter published Long Short-Term Memory, a recurrent neural network architecture that overcame the vanishing gradient problem and became one of the most widely used designs in speech recognition and language modeling before the rise of Transformers. He has long served as Scientific Director of the Swiss AI Lab IDSIA, and since 2021 has also directed the AI Initiative at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology. He co-founded NNAISENSE, a company applying his lab's neural network research to industrial and robotic systems.

achievements.title: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), 1997
